overview: The Medford Conservation Commission oversees the protection of wetland resource areas and floodplains through the review of Notices of Intent and the issuance of environmental permits. The commission has been meeting regularly from December 2024 through October 2026 to evaluate projects ranging from large-scale riverfront redevelopments to residential additions. Key areas of focus include stormwater management, tree preservation, and the management of invasive species in protected zones. As of the most recent meetings, the commission is actively drafting stricter local wetlands protection regulations and reviewing trail rehabilitation projects in the Middlesex Fells.

threads.name: Route 28 Pathway and Boardwalk
threads.summary: The commission initially reviewed plans for a multi-use connection near the Route 28 Fellsway bridge, requesting detailed planting plans and alternatives to tropical hardwood. The project was approved in early 2025 with a condition requiring a pre-construction operations and maintenance plan. In 2026, the commission received a pre-construction update regarding the removal and replacement of dead and diseased trees along the project site.

threads.name: 97-99 Revere Beach Parkway Redevelopment
threads.summary: A proposal to transform the former KISS 108 radio station site into a 352,400-square-foot multi-family residential building was introduced in mid-2025. Commissioners scrutinized the project's groundwater data, stormwater level spreaders, and invasive species management. The project was ultimately approved with special conditions for porous pavement, preservation of existing black locust and birch groves, and public greenway access along the Malden River.

threads.name: Drafting Local Wetlands Regulations
threads.summary: Following concerns about potential state-level permit exemptions under the Mass Ready Act, the commission began a comprehensive review of new local wetlands protection regulations in 2026. These draft rules propose stricter standards than state law, including a two-to-one wetland replication ratio and a 25-foot no-activity buffer zone. The commission also explored tree replacement formulas and a potential ban on coal tar-based drive sealants, with further review sessions planned.

threads.name: Middlesex Fells Reservation Projects
threads.summary: The commission frequently reviews ecological and infrastructure work within the Middlesex Fells, including the closeout of a 2014 stream crossing project. In 2026, the body approved invasive species management at the 90-millimeter meadow to restore pollinator habitat. Most recently, the commission issued an Order of Conditions for trail rehabilitation and bridge replacement along the Cross Fells and Skyline trails.

threads.name: Infrastructure and Stormwater Management
threads.summary: The commission evaluated several road and parking projects where flooding was a primary concern for abutters. A parking lot expansion on Sycamore Avenue was approved only after the applicant reduced the number of spaces to preserve mature trees and increased compensatory flood storage. Similarly, improvements to Mystic River Road were approved with specific conditions to protect existing tree roots during grading.

threads.name: Residential Additions and Compliance
threads.summary: Private property improvements, such as a retaining wall on Wentworth Road and additions on Arlington Street, required commission oversight to ensure permanent barriers between yards and wetlands. The commission typically conditions these approvals on the use of native vegetation and the installation of wetland signage. In some cases, such as at 54 South Street, the commission conducted site visits to verify that required plantings met density and quantity standards.

threads.name: Public and Municipal Projects
threads.summary: The commission reviews municipal maintenance and improvements, such as a five-year vegetation management plan for the MBTA commuter rail right-of-way. It issued negative determinations for pavement and lighting repairs at the Condon Shell and drainage improvements on the Mustang Loop Trail. In late 2026, the commission also approved a certificate of compliance for ADA accessibility modifications and dugout replacement at Veterans Memorial Park.

periods.narrative: This period focused on major residential and infrastructure developments, including the approval of the Route 28 boardwalk and the Revere Beach Parkway multi-family complex.
The commission shifted its attention toward strengthening local environmental protections through new bylaws and managing several habitat restoration projects in the Middlesex Fells.
